rationale_summary: Four personas include rucaparib as the registered all-comer PARP that replicates the PRIMA signal in an independent phase 3 (ATHENA-MONO, n=538): the critic ranks it second on evidence quality, and the concensusite, conservative, and advocate all carry it as an oral maintenance option. The benefit holds in the intent-to-treat population (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.40-0.68 from the primary JCO publication, pmid:35658487) rather than resting on a BRCA-mutant subgroup, which is what qualifies a BRCA-wild-type tumor. No persona vetoed or dissented, so it carries the cleanest board signal on the list (agreement_score 0.8). The same severe-myelosuppression veto that shadows niraparib applies here (grade 3+ anemia 28.7%), so it is no toxicity escape: the advocate frames the marrow risk as the patient's to lift, and the conservative would endorse it only with serial CBC and LFT monitoring. It lacks the tumor-partitioning pharmacology that points niraparib specifically at this BRCA-proficient biology, which is the one reason niraparib is not simply redundant with it.
open_questions: No tumor-partitioning or trapping pharmacology pointing rucaparib specifically at this BRCA-proficient biology, unlike niraparib
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high for PFS: replicated all-comer phase 3 (ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52, 20.2 vs 9.2 mo) qualifying a BRCA-wild-type tumor without a BRCA or GIS gate.

counter_productive_moa.description: PARP myelosuppression is a patient-AE burden, not a mechanism that blunts the maintenance goal in genomically-unstable HGSC.

overall: Replicated all-comer PARP maintenance that qualifies a BRCA-wild-type tumor with no GIS gate; near-interchangeable with niraparib but lacks its tumor-specific pharmacology, and carries the same myelosuppression veto.

rationale_summary: Four of five personas (risktaker, conservative, critic, concensusite) call niraparib the cleanest efficacy and guideline fit: PRIMA is a registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 whose all-comer enrolment is the eligibility match itself for a BRCA-wild-type, genomically-unstable tumor — no cross-stratum extrapolation needed. The risktaker adds the only tumor-specific argument on the board: niraparib partitioned into tumor at 3.3x plasma and cut growth 58% in a BRCA-wild-type PDX where olaparib barely moved (pmid:30647846). It ranks below rucaparib only because of where the veto and dissent signal landed. The conservative issued a CONDITIONAL veto — against ranking niraparib at rank 1 on the patient's own myelosuppression veto — that it will withdraw once a hematology-supported, platelet-based starting-dose plan and a written cytopenia-management pathway are on file; the advocate dissented for the same reason, holding that the veto is the patient's to lift, not the board's to rank past on evidence. We override the veto to keep niraparib ranked and visible (per the no-silent-drop rule) but carry it at considered_with_caveats: the all-comer benefit is real and PFS-grade (OS immature, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.44-1.11), and the larger HRD-positive effect (HR 0.43) does NOT apply without a validated score.

rationale_summary: The conservative, advocate, and concensusite lead with bevacizumab for the same patient-side reason: it is the only maintenance axis on the board that clears both named vetoes outright — no added neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression — on a backbone she already tolerates, FDA-approved since 2014 with more than a decade of post-marketing follow-up. The critic ranks it third and insists it be labelled a PFS hold rather than a survival argument: GOG-218 and ICON7 show no overall-population OS benefit. The risktaker dissents on magnitude — leading with the smallest effect on the board (HR 0.717) for an efficacy-leaning (0.7) patient forfeits the larger PARP signal and banks a curve she is already riding. The operative caution is VTE/bleeding against her IVC-filter history, which the conservative and advocate both manage with established BP and bleeding monitoring rather than escalation. The advocate's only quarrel is sequencing — the patient asked for the confirmatory workup first — which is a round-2 dissent about ordering, not an objection to the drug.

rationale_summary: The conservative, concensusite, and advocate all keep letrozole as the gentlest option in front of the board — oral, once-daily, no infusion burden, and it trips none of her vetoes, which suits the 70-79 age band and her oral preference. Its agreement_score ties rucaparib's at 0.6 because nobody objected, but the evidence is the weakest on the list: pmid:29157627 is a non-randomized retrospective comparison nested in a translational ER-expression study (ROBINS-I serious, tier 4, n=80), and the critic insists the ROBINS-I Serious tag sit next to the rank so a reader does not take the 60% for a trial result. The clinician also flagged a design mismatch — the trials row described a single-arm phase 2, but the source is a retrospective translational series. PR-negativity predicts a more modest response than the ~80% ER reading alone suggests. It is the low-toxicity floor — a later-line or adjunct fallback, not a substitute for a randomized-backed maintenance regimen.

overall: The lowest-toxicity oral option that clears every veto and fits the age band, but the evidence is a single retrospective ROBINS-I-serious series and PR-negativity tempers the expected magnitude.

rationale_summary: This is the highest-magnitude maintenance on the board (HRD-positive HR 0.33), and the patient is already on the bevacizumab half — but it ranks last for two distinct, both-live reasons. The critic dissented on evidence quality — the load-bearing HR 0.33 is a pre-specified subgroup (ITT HR 0.59) and the patient does not clear the companion-diagnostic gate that defines it — and the advocate dissented on the stacked PARP-plus-anti-angiogenic toxicity against the IVC-filter history. We override the conservative veto and keep the row at considered_with_caveats (no silent drop) because the risktaker and concensusite hold it as a contingent high-upside option: a Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS >=42 opens the eligibility gate and makes the toxicity veto addressable. guideline_status: Not NCCN/ESMO/SGO-endorsed for HER2-low ovarian; the tumor-agnostic T-DXd approval requires IHC 3+, so it is off-guideline and investigational at IHC 1+.
rationale_summary: The HER2-low (IHC 1+) finding adds a genuinely HER2-directed option, and the advocate, critic, and risktaker all carry it — but only as an investigational, relapse-context choice, never as approved standard care. The tumor-agnostic trastuzumab deruxtecan approval requires IHC 3+; this tumor is IHC 1+, so the case rests on cross-tumor extrapolation from HER2-low breast (DESTINY-Breast04 HR+ PFS HR 0.51, DESTINY-Breast06 HER2-low PFS HR 0.62) plus the DXd bystander mechanism, with the only ovarian cohort (PanTumor02, ORR 45%) enrolled at IHC 2+/3+ above her tier. The advocate carries it because, unlike disitamab vedotin, its ILD-and-nausea profile clears both named vetoes; the concensusite dissented on guideline fit, since no society endorses HER2-directed therapy in HER2-low ovarian. The critic and risktaker agree it is a relapse option, not a current maintenance pick — the critic's round-2 dissent was against the risktaker ranking it as high as third on a mechanism argument standing in for absent ovarian data. Two practical brakes keep it low: it is IV q3w against the low-infusion preference with a 10-12% ILD rate that has been fatal, and the IHC 1+ call rests on a single specimen Altera could not stain, so a confirmatory re-stain comes first. Per Hard Rule 6 it is ranked, not foreclosed, at considered_with_caveats with explicit investigational status.

likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate, cross-tumor only: no ovarian IHC 1+ data; rests on HER2-low breast extrapolation (DESTINY-Breast04 PFS HR 0.51) plus the DXd bystander mechanism.
toxicity_burden: High (ILD/pneumonitis 10-12% incl. fatal cases; grade 3+ AE 52.6%; nausea; anemia)

counter_productive_moa.description: Bystander DXd reach is unproven at IHC 1+ antigen density; sparse HER2-positive cells may not seed enough payload to kill neighbors.

overall: The one HER2-directed option that clears both named vetoes, but investigational at IHC 1+ ovarian on breast-only extrapolation — a relapse consideration after a confirmatory re-stain, not a maintenance pick.

rationale_summary: All five personas rejected disitamab vedotin, so it is kept here as not_recommended rather than dropped, so the reader sees what was considered and why. Its MMAE payload runs peripheral sensory neuropathy at 68.2% any-grade and 18.7% grade 3+ plus neutropenia at 12.1% grade 3+ (urothelial safety read, pmid:37988648), which hits both of the patient's named vetoes — additional peripheral neuropathy and severe myelosuppression — head-on, with no mitigation on offer. On biomarker and tumor type the open solid-tumor basket (NCT06003231) does accept HER2 IHC 1+ ovarian, so it is the most directly enrollable HER2 option in the set, which is exactly why the board documented its rejection rather than ignoring it. The only published HER2-low efficacy datapoint is an abstract-only, PAM-pathway-selected breast series (ORR ~34%), with no ovarian data. The accessibility pass also flags that the US basket is now active-not-recruiting and the only recruiting trial is China-only, so there is no current enrollment route regardless. It is excluded on a unanimous toxicity veto, not on a contingent or evidence-only basis.
